results.rationale: Platinum anomalies at Middle-East sites (e.g., Abu Hureyra, Syria) are among the more independently corroborated YDIH proxies, while impact-driven population-demography claims in Mexico remain speculative and weakly evidenced (model-prior).

Population-demographic collapse claims tied to the impact are widely contested/unsupported so a 'refuted' framing is plausible, whereas nanodiamond concentration claims have faced substantial independent-lab replication failures, making a 'triggered' assertion less credible (model-prior).

Megafaunal extinction being driven by the impact is a heavily disputed causal claim (overkill/climate hypotheses dominate), while a Greenland ice-sheet platinum spike at the YD onset is one of the more replicated proxy findings (model-prior).

The absence of a confirmed matching impact crater is a genuine, oft-cited critique of YDIH (though the stated interval is oddly offset), whereas iridium anomalies specifically have shown weaker/less consistent replication than platinum across sites (model-prior).

Refuting impact-driven YD cooling aligns with the mainstream preference for meltwater/AMOC-forcing explanations and is a well-documented counter-argument, somewhat stronger than the more narrowly debated population-demography refutation claim (model-prior).

Both microspherule and melt-glass claims are contested in the literature (spherules often reattributed to fungal/anthropogenic sources; melt-glass reports are rarer but somewhat more robust at specific sites), yielding a roughly even, slightly B-leaning assessment (model-prior).

Impact-triggered YD cooling is a core, extensively debated YDIH claim, whereas melt-glass formation is a terrestrial high-heat phenomenon rarely if ever reported within ice-sheet cores, making B's specific placement less geologically plausible (model-prior).

Impact-driven population-demography shifts in North America lack strong supporting evidence, while refutation of impact-driven biomass-burning/impact-winter as the YD cooling trigger aligns with mainstream critiques of continental-scale charcoal/soot evidence (model-prior).
